questions.question: A region is characterized under dry farming if the annual rainfall in that region less then
questions.explanation: Cultivation of crops where rainfall is less than 750 mm per annum is called as a dry farming. Dry farming regions are arid regions of the country[cite: 15].

questions.question: Identify which of the following is a characteristic of region under dry farming?
questions.explanation: Main features of this region i. Prolonged dry spells are very common during crop period. ii. More frequent crop failures. iii. High Evo transpiration (moisture loss) iv. Very low moisture presents in soil. v. Less socio-economic development. vi. High saline soil vii. Cropping period is highly dependent on the rainfall[cite: 15].

questions.question: Western Rajasthan and Bundelkhand region come under ___ type farming based on amount of rainfall that region.
questions.explanation: Dry Farming: Cultivation of crops where rainfall is less than 750 mm per annum is called as a dry farming. Dry farming regions are arid regions of the country. Major regions of dry farming in India - western Rajasthan, Bundelkhand region, Gujarat & all the arid regions.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Dryland farming is a region which receives ___ amount of rainfall per annum.
questions.explanation: Cultivation of crops in area receiving rainfall above 750-1150 mm per annum is called as dryland farming. Dryland farming is practiced in all the semiarid regions of the country.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh come under ___ farming region based on the amount of rainfall they receive per annum.
questions.explanation: Major regions where dryland farming is practiced- Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil nandu, Andhra Pradesh and all the semi-arid regions of the country.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Cultivation of crops in region receiving ___ mm per annum rainfall is called as rainfed farming.
questions.explanation: Cultivation of crops in regions receiving more than 1150 mm annually is known as rainfed farming.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of rainfed farming?

options.a: Acidic soil is the major constrain

questions.explanation: Main features of this region: Crop failure is very rare. Very rare or no dry spell. Waterlogging/ drainage is major problem. Acidic soil is a constrain.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Which of the following is the major constrain of dryland agriculture?
questions.explanation: Problems & Constrains in Dryland Agriculture: Less or lack of proper moisture for cultivating crops is the major constrain in dryland agriculture. High temperature with Very low or erratic rainfall. Low water table so very less irrigation facility like tubewell, canals etc. Degraded soil due to very less organic matter in the soil. Less fertile soil, less nutrient present in soil. High PET (potential evo transpiration rate) means high water[cite: 15]

questions.question: According to the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), a meteorological drought is defined as a condition when the rainfall in a region decreases by ___
questions.explanation: It refers to the substantial deficit or rainfall relative to the average of that region. According to the IMD meteorological drought is a condition when there is 25% decrease in the rainfall for a given period of time in a region.[cite: 15]

questions.question: ___ refers to the extended dry period in which lack of rainfall results in insufficient moisture in the root zone causing crop loss
questions.explanation: Agriculture drought- It refers to the extended dry period in which lack of rainfall results in insufficient moisture in the root zone of the soil causing adverse effects on crop.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Rainless period of less then ___ days in heavy soil is called dry spell.
questions.explanation: Dry spell - rainless period more than 10 days in light soil (sandy) areas and 15 days in heavy soil (clay) areas. Drought- it is prolonged dry spell resulting wilting or drying of crops[cite: 15]

questions.question: ___ when the soil moisture reaches to -15 bar, plants show wilting symptom during the day but not die is called as
questions.explanation: Permanent wilting point - when the soil moisture reaches to -15 bar, plants show wilting symptom during the day but not die. Ultimate wilting point- when the soil moisture reaches -6 MPa or -60 bar plant will die due to moisture stress.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Which of the following method are used to conserve soil moisture in dry land agriculture?
questions.explanation: Reducing runoff- water runoff increases when there is high intensity of rainfall due to low infiltration, so more opportunity time should be provided to the runoff water to increase the rate of infiltration. Application of farm yard manure increase the soil moisture by increasing soil water holding capacity. Disc ploughing during summer and contour bunding enhances the soil moisture storage in the soil. Increase rate of infiltration by maintaining mulches and addition of crop residue in fields.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Which of the following measure is not adopted to conserve the soil moisture in dry land agriculture?

options.e: All of the above are used

questions.explanation: All of the above are used to conserve the soil moisture in dry land agriculture Tillage increases the water holding capacity, reduces runoff, increases infiltration & conserve soil moisture.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Phenyl mercuric acetate is a ___ type of anti-transpirant?
questions.explanation: Stomata Closing- Stomata closing anti-transpirant function by closing the stomatal pores present on the leaves surface from which maximum transpiration occurs Examples-phenyl mercuric acetate and atrazine[cite: 15]

questions.question: Identify which of the following is a film forming type of Anti-transpirants?
questions.explanation: Film Forming Type- The mode of action of film forming antitranspirant is that they form a thin waxy layer on the leaf surface and retard the escape of water from the leaves by formation of a physical barrier. Examples- mobileaf, hexadecanol, silicone etc. Reflectant type - 5 per cent kaolin spray, diatomaceous earth product (celite) etc Growth retardants - Cycocel is one such chemical useful for improving water status of the plant.[cite: 15]

questions.question: What is the major disadvantage of using anti transpirant?
questions.explanation: Antitranspirants generally reduce photosynthesis. Therefore, their use is limited to save the crop from death under severe moisture stress. If crop survives, it can utilize the rainfall that is received subsequently.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Which of the following crops can be grown in arid and semi-arid region effectively?
questions.explanation: Major Crops Cultivated in Dryland Conditions Millets- such as bajra, ragi, sorghum etc. Oilseeds- mustard, rapeseed, groundnut etc. Pulse crops- pigeon pea, gram and lentil, soyabean, moong, chick pea etc. Almost 80% of maize and Jowar, 90 per cent of Bajra and approximately 95% of pulses and 75% of oilseeds are obtained from dryland agriculture.[cite: 15]

questions.question: What is the approximate total area under the rainfed agricultural system in India?
questions.explanation: Area under irrigated and rainfed conditions in India Class Area (m ha) Total arable = 143.8 Dryland = 34.5 Rainfed = 65.5 Irrigated = 43.8[cite: 15]

questions.question: What were the twin initiative of the national watershed development plan for the rainfed area which was launched in 1990-91?

options.a: Integrated watershed management and sustainable farming systems.
options.b: Rain water harvesting and watershed management
options.c: Promotion of Micro irrigation and sustainable farming system
options.d: Promotion of rain water harvesting and sustainable farming system

questions.explanation: National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA)- The scheme of National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA) was launched in 1990-91 based on twin concepts of integrated watershed management and sustainable farming systems.[cite: 15]

questions.question: Which of the following crops are suitable to grow in dryland regions of India?
questions.explanation: Major Crops Cultivated in Dryland Conditions Millets- such as bajra, ragi, sorghum etc. Oilseeds- mustard, rapeseed, groundnut etc. Pulse crops- pigeon pea, gram and lentil, soyabean, moong, chick pea etc. Almost 80% of maize and Jowar, 90 per cent of Bajra and approximately 95% of pulses and 75% of oilseeds are obtained from dryland agriculture.[cite: 15]
